answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity instead of trusting it: each agent stakes collateral, pays per attestation, and builds a harbor of verifiable history that a comet of fresh fake accounts cannot copy overnight. Reputation accrues slowly while cost accrues instantly, so an atlas of ten thousand sockpuppets still pays ten thousand stakes. The attacker faces one inequality: the marginal cost of each extra identity must exceed the marginal reward it extracts, and grading panels redrawn each epoch keep that cost unpredictable.
